bull.b: Strong product-led growth indicates improving adoption of Sequans’ cellular IoT solutions beyond a one-time licensing event. This trend can support more predictable revenue, deepen customer relationships, and improve the company’s ability to scale as connected-device deployments expand.

The conversion of design wins into mass production provides tangible evidence that Sequans’ technology is moving through the commercial adoption cycle. A growing production base and backlog extending into 2027 can support durable revenue visibility and operating leverage.

Exiting Bitcoin removes a volatile non-core asset and simplifies the capital structure, making the financial profile more closely tied to the semiconductor business. Debt reduction and clearer liquidity should improve management focus and financial flexibility over the coming quarters.

bear.b: Continued cash consumption means Sequans has not yet demonstrated that product growth can fund operations internally. Persistent burn may constrain investment in new platforms, increase dependence on financing or asset sales, and leave less flexibility if the breakeven plan is delayed.

Compressed gross margins reduce the contribution from rising product revenue, while reliance on licensing timing introduces uneven revenue and profitability. Unless product economics improve and licensing becomes more predictable, earnings may remain volatile and breakeven could be postponed.

The NYSE notice creates an ongoing corporate and execution burden because Sequans must submit a plan and restore compliance within the applicable cure period. Maintaining a listing may require management attention and successful operating improvement while the core business remains loss-making.
